name: draft-to-living-cell
title: From Draft to Living Cell
lead: A cellular interface is not just a modeler's simplification — it is a testable hypothesis about which interactions matter, and staying alive is what makes the boundary real. A cell is a self-maintaining, adaptive agent exactly to the extent that it holds its exchange variables inside a viability bound; crossing that bound is what forces a model — and the biology it represents — to be cut open and re-described at another grain. This investigation follows the paper's own arc across 9 studies, each written first as an inert typed draft and then compiled into a running executable that preserves the interface exactly, from the interface itself through where it holds, where it fails, and how it is rebuilt at another level. The flagship exhibit is Disintegration (Fig 6) — a viability collapse that can be played step by step, plus the same metabolic interface realized at three grains — coarse, kinetic, and real COBRApy flux-balance — behind ports that never move.

at_a_glance.role: Fig 4's typed cell contract compiled to a bounded, goal-directed cell — chemical, mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports plus growth, shape, objective, and viability. Home of law 1 conformance: the one impostor handler in this codebase is rejected at compile time with a CompileError naming the missing ports; that impostor lives in the metabolism code, cross-referenced from disintegration.

Fig 5's sense/act loop closed over a real diffusing spatial field — the cell depletes and reshapes the very chemical gradient it depends on (niche construction), interface preserved unchanged (law 2).

No figure of its own — two cells wired over one shared nutrient store negotiate viability: competition starves the weaker cell while the stronger persists; a different handler over the identical interface (cross-feeding) keeps both alive (law 4).

The flagship (Fig 6) — playable: a level-shift you can step through — thermal shock, viability collapse, biomass turning to debris. Structural: the cell-to-molecular-network grain-swap, carrying coarse, kinetic, and real COBRApy FBA metabolism behind one interface that never moves (law 4).

Fig 7's F1Fo ATP-synthase mechanism drives all four physical channels — chemical, electrical, mechanical, thermal — from one coupled proton flux; a molecular grain of the kind disintegration drops into, made concrete.

Fig 8's six-level nested place graph (membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, chromosome, chromatin, nucleosome) with a coupled gene-expression cascade wired to the deepest leaf; interface preserved at the deepest nesting (law 2). Selectivity is narrated, assembly is demonstrated.

Fig 9's metabolism, containment, and replication compile into mutual closure toward a minimal cell — law 4's second grain-swap home. The closure pattern, demonstrated qualitatively, not validated autopoiesis.

Fig 10a,b — growth (autocatalytic, energy-coupled) drives the cell's own DNA past a threshold; crossing it fires a genuine place-graph rewrite, one cell node becoming two, mass conserved (parent halved, not duplicated) — law 2'.

Fig 10c-f — biofilm nesting and port-addition/selection as event-driven rewrites, including genuine node-inserting "Live Topology" pairs. Explicitly caveated pattern demos (gate: needs_calibration) — the paper itself calls this transition "an open and substantial challenge."

how_to_read:
Read the 9 studies in the paper's own order — cellular-interface, cell-environment-
coupling, cell-cell-coupling, disintegration, molecular-interfaces, biomolecular-complementarity,
autopoiesis, growth-and-division, development-and-evolution — the arc runs from the interface
itself, through where it couples and where it breaks, down to the molecular mechanisms that
maintain it, and back up through growth, division, and the harder, honestly-caveated
transitions of development and evolution.

In each study, look at two things side by side: the draft render (the loom figure — the
structural interface, no dynamics) and the executable dynamics (the same interface, now
running). The investigation's sharpest control is the compiler's impostor-rejection, exercised
in the cellular-interface/disintegration metabolism code: a handler that breaks the port
contract is refused at compile time with a CompileError naming the missing ports — that is the
interface being enforced, not merely described.

Short on time? Read cellular-interface (the contract and law 1's impostor rejection),
disintegration (the flagship — playable viability collapse plus the three-grain metabolism
swap), and growth-and-division (a genuine structural rewrite). Then skim the capstone below for
the same grain-swap carried up to a whole cell. Throughout, hold the compiler's law 2: did the
mechanism change while the structural interface — port names, types, wiring — stayed the same?
And hold the throughline: did the study build, test, break, or rebuild a viability boundary?

glossary.definition: The set of typed, unit-bearing variables through which a cellular description couples to its environment and to other cells (fluxes, forces, currents, heat, plus growth, shape, objective, viability) — simultaneously a modeling choice and a testable hypothesis about which interactions matter.
An interface with a structural contract but no dynamics — typed ports + wiring + intent, an inert (empty) update; it builds and renders but does nothing if run.
An executable Process that implements a draft's interface with real dynamics; the compiler installs one per draft.

Structural conformance — a handler conforms to a signature when it supplies every interface port with a compatible type and wiring; the compiler refuses to install a non-conforming handler. It checks port names, types, and wiring — not units, dimensions, invariants, or runtime behavior.
Compilation changes a study's internal mechanism but leaves its external interface — port names and wired store paths — identical.
Realizing one interface at a different level of description (a lumped process vs. a resolved network) without changing the interface — disintegration's Fig 6, and autopoiesis's second home.
A composition whose processes collectively produce and sustain the very organization that enables them — autopoiesis (Fig 9)'s mutual closure of metabolism, containment, and replication.
The region of state space within which a cellular description stays valid; crossing them (e.g. a thermal shock) breaks the interface and forces a shift to a molecular description.

The property an interface confers on what would otherwise be ordinary chemical dynamics — the capacity to sense, act, and maintain a boundary against dissolution — for as long as its variables stay inside the viability bound. The investigation's throughline.

A discrete change to the place graph itself — division, engulfment, bursting, biofilm colonization — that adds or removes nodes at runtime (growth-and-division, Fig 10a,b; development-and-evolution's "Live Topology" pairs, Fig 10c-f).
The nesting of stores in the state tree; the bigraph structure that represents compartments and containment.

biological_story:
A cell is two things at once. From the outside it is a bounded, goal-directed agent
that exchanges matter, energy, and information with its environment and with other cells across
a small set of interface variables, and stays alive only while those variables sit inside its
viability bounds. From the inside it is a dense web of coupled molecular processes that build
and maintain the very interface the outside view depends on. Neither view is complete alone,
and the paper's central claim is that the interface connecting them is not merely a modeling
convenience — it is a testable hypothesis about which interactions actually matter to the cell's
fate.

This investigation walks the paper's own arc, and at every step the same discipline applies:
first draw the *interface* (the ports through which a process couples to the rest of the cell),
commit to no mechanism yet, and only then install one. We begin at the cellular interface itself
(cellular-interface, Fig 4) — chemical, mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports plus
higher-level cellular variables like growth rate, shape, objective, and viability, and the first
home of law 1: a non-conforming handler is rejected at compile time. We make the interface
operational by closing the loop with the environment (cell-environment-coupling, Fig 5) — the
cell senses a real diffusing field and acts back on it, reshaping the gradient it depends on —
and then by coupling it to another cell over one shared resource (cell-cell-coupling): the same
interface, wired twice, negotiates viability between two agents, not just state.

Composition is not only about connecting. It is equally about knowing when to cut the model open.
When a cell's viability bound is crossed, the cellular description stops being valid and the
right level of description drops to molecules — disintegration (Fig 6), the investigation's
flagship, plays that collapse step by step and shows the same metabolic interface surviving three
grains of resolution: a coarse lumped yield, a saturating kinetic law, and a real COBRApy
flux-balance optimization. We then follow that molecular level down further — a single ATP-
synthase mechanism honoring all four physical channels (molecular-interfaces, Fig 7) — and back
up into architecture — molecules nested six levels into complexes, organelles, and a bounded cell
(biomolecular-complementarity, Fig 8). We ask how a maintained interface arises from molecular
processes in the first place: metabolism, containment, and replication mutually closing into a
minimal cell (autopoiesis, Fig 9) — the closure that Maturana and Varela called autopoiesis,
demonstrated here as a pattern, not a validated result.

Finally, that organization is rewritten across time. Growth drives a cell's own DNA past a
threshold and division fires as a genuine, mass-conserving structural rewrite — one cell node
becoming two (growth-and-division, Fig 10a,b). Cells then nest into a biofilm and lineages
acquire new interface capabilities (development-and-evolution, Fig 10c-f) — the paper's own
"open and substantial challenge," honestly caveated here rather than overclaimed.

Underneath every study is the same throughline: viability bounds and minimal agency. An interface
is what turns ordinary chemical dynamics into a self-maintaining, adaptive agent, and every study
in this investigation either builds that boundary, tests it, breaks it, or rebuilds it at another
grain. A closing capstone carries the disintegration grain-swap up to one hand-assembled whole
cell — coarse, kinetic, and real-FBA metabolism behind one interface give three distinct life
histories, and each cell grows, divides once (mass conserved), and dies when a scripted thermal
shock pushes it outside its viable band. A cell that lives and dies, with the mechanism of its
life swappable behind a fixed boundary — and the boundary itself is what the paper asks us to take
seriously as biology, not just as software.
question:
Is a cellular interface simultaneously a modeling choice — a decision about which
ports matter, what units they carry, how a process couples to the rest of the cell — and a
testable biological hypothesis about which interactions actually govern a cell's fate? And
does treating composition as an ongoing practice — connect two interfaces where their
assumptions hold, cut the model open at the interface when those assumptions fail, coarse-grain
a resolved network back into a lumped exchange when organization re-emerges — let the same
cellular specification hold together across environment coupling, cell-cell coupling,
molecular mechanism, nested complementarity, autopoietic closure, growth, division, and the
harder transitions of development and evolution, while tracking viability bounds as the
locus of minimal agency throughout?
hypothesis:
Every recurring composition pattern in the cellular-interface paper — the typed
contract, environment coupling, cell-cell coupling, the disintegration/grain-swap that cuts
the model open at the interface, the molecular mechanism, nested complementarity, autopoietic
closure, growth-driven division, and the developmental/evolutionary rewrite — can be authored
as an inert draft (typed, unit-bearing ports + a structural contract, with no dynamics) and
then *compiled* — by installing one conforming mechanism per draft — into an executable that
preserves the paper's interface exactly and produces genuine dynamics. Across the 9 studies,
the interface is the site where ordinary chemical dynamics becomes a self-maintaining,
viability-bounded agent, and composition — connecting, cutting open, coarse-graining — is how
that boundary is built, tested, and maintained.

executive.what_is_this:
This investigation turns *A meta-modeler's guide to the cellular interface* into an executable test of the paper's central claim: a cellular interface is simultaneously a modeling choice and a testable biological hypothesis about which interactions govern a cell's fate. Each study is written twice. First as a draft: a typed, unit-bearing interface — a structural contract of port names, types, and wiring, with no committed mechanism. It says what a process couples to, not how. Then it is compiled, which installs one or more conforming mechanisms — mechanistic, rule-based, data-driven, or otherwise — behind the identical ports, so the running simulation preserves the declared interface exactly. This operationalizes the paper's R_L (the process- implementation relation) and the Discussion's semantic-to-executable layer: a draft is the semantic layer, and compilation is the step that gives it an executable one. The compiler's conformance check is structural only: it verifies that a handler supplies every port with a compatible type and wiring, and refuses one that does not. It does not check units, dimensions, invariants, or runtime behavior.

The point is not to assemble one monolithic cell model. It is to test whether composition is an ongoing practice rather than a final architecture: connect two interfaces where their assumptions hold (cell-environment and cell-cell coupling), cut the model open at the interface when those assumptions fail and the right level of description drops to molecules (disintegration — the paper's Fig 6, and this investigation's flagship), and coarse-grain a resolved molecular network back into a lumped exchange when organization re-emerges (the same pattern run in reverse, and again in autopoiesis). Underneath every study sits one throughline: viability bounds and minimal agency. A cellular description is valid only while its interface variables sit inside a viability bound; the interface is the locus where ordinary chemical dynamics becomes a self-maintaining, adaptive agent, and losing that boundary is exactly what disintegration demonstrates.

The 9 studies below follow the paper's own order: the cellular interface itself, then where it couples to environment and to other cells, then where it breaks (disintegration) and what it is made of underneath (molecular interfaces, biomolecular complementarity, autopoiesis), then how it is rewritten across time (growth and division, development and evolution). A closing capstone carries the disintegration grain-swap up to one hand-assembled whole cell that grows, divides, and dies; a coverage note confirms that every figure draft in this investigation compiles to a running executable.
executive.verdict:
The reading holds, and it runs, across all 9 studies in the paper's order. The interface
is a testable hypothesis, not just a convenience: cellular-interface (Fig 4) compiles a typed
contract into a bounded, goal-directed cell, and home to law 1 conformance — the one concrete
impostor handler in this codebase (a non-conforming metabolism that renames/drops ports) is
rejected by the compiler at compile time with a CompileError naming the missing ports; that
impostor itself lives in the metabolism/Fig 6 code, cross-referenced here from disintegration.
Cell-environment coupling (Fig 5) closes a genuine sense/act loop over a real diffusing spatial
field — niche construction, not scripted (law 2). Cell-cell coupling (no figure of its own) shows
that composing two cell interfaces over one shared nutrient store couples constraint, not just
state: competition starves the weaker cell while the stronger persists; a different handler over
the same interface (cross-feeding) keeps both alive (law 4).

The flagship is Disintegration (Fig 6): playable — a scripted thermal shock collapses viability,
halts viability-gated metabolism, and turns biomass into molecular debris, watchable step by step
in the Composite Explorer — and structural: the same metabolic-exchange interface is realized at
three grains (a coarse lumped yield, a saturating Michaelis-Menten kinetic, and real COBRApy
flux-balance optimization over e_coli_core) behind ports that never move — the cell-to-molecular-
network grain-swap that carries coarse, kinetic, and real-FBA behavior behind one interface
(law 4).

Molecular interfaces (Fig 7) drops one level further: an F1Fo ATP-synthase mechanism drives all
four physical channels — chemical, electrical, mechanical, thermal — from one coupled proton
flux, honoring the four-channel contract — an example of the kind of molecular grain
disintegration drops into.
Biomolecular complementarity (Fig 8) nests six place-graph levels deep with a coupled gene-
expression cascade wired to the deepest leaf, and the interface survives that nesting — law 2's
deepest test in this codebase; complementarity/selectivity is narrated as the paper's organizing
idea, but hierarchical assembly is what the executable demonstrates, not a binding-affinity
mechanism. Autopoiesis (Fig 9) compiles metabolism, containment, and replication into mutual
closure toward a minimal cell — law 4's second grain-swap home — but this is the closure pattern
demonstrated qualitatively, not a validated autopoietic system.

Growth and division (Fig 10a,b) is the sharpest structural result: an autocatalytic, energy-
coupled growth process drives the cell's own DNA past a threshold, and crossing it fires a
genuine place-graph rewrite — one cell node becomes two, mass conserved (the parent is halved,
not duplicated) — law 2' (rewrite conformance) alongside law 2 (interface preserved across the
rewrite). Development and evolution (Fig 10c-f) is explicitly caveated: biofilm nesting and
port-addition/selection compile and run as event-driven rewrites, and a "Live Topology" pair for
each genuinely inserts and removes place-graph nodes, but selection is a single ODE with fixed
constants and the "new port" a scripted config ramp — this study's own gate is needs_calibration,
and the paper itself calls this transition "an open and substantial challenge."

Finally, a capstone assembled by hand (not compiler-emitted) carries the disintegration grain-swap
up to a whole cell — coarse, kinetic, and real-FBA metabolism behind one interface give three
distinct life histories, and each cell grows, divides once (mass-conserved), and dies on a
scripted thermal shock. Same law, one level up.
decisions_needed: development-and-evolution's own gate is needs_calibration: selection is a single fixed-constant ODE and the "new port" a scripted config ramp, not emergent population or fitness dynamics. Treat its results as pattern demonstrations only until replaced with genuine, state-driven selection and innovation mechanisms.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
A cellular interface is simultaneously a modeling choice and a testable biological
hypothesis about which interactions govern a cell's fate: each of the paper's compositional
patterns can be authored as an inert typed draft (an interface with no committed mechanism) and
then compiled — by installing a conforming mechanism — into a running model whose *external
interface is preserved unchanged*. Composition is not a fixed final architecture but an ongoing
practice — connect where assumptions hold, cut the model open at the interface when they fail,
coarse-grain when organization re-emerges — and the interface itself is the locus where chemical
dynamics becomes a self-maintaining, viability-bounded agent.
evidence_for: cellular-interface (Fig 4) — the cell's typed, unit-bearing exchange ports (chemical, mechanical, electrical, thermal) plus growth, shape, objective, and viability compile into a bounded, goal-directed cell. Home of law 1 conformance: the one impostor handler in this codebase (a non-conforming metabolism) is rejected at compile time with a CompileError naming the missing ports; the impostor itself lives in the metabolism/disintegration code, cross-referenced here.

cell-environment-coupling (Fig 5) — the interface closes into a genuine sense/act loop over a real diffusing spatial field; the cell measurably reshapes the gradient it depends on (niche construction), interface preserved unchanged (law 2).

cell-cell-coupling (no figure of its own) — two cells coupled over one shared nutrient interface negotiate viability, not just state: competition starves the weaker cell while the stronger persists; cross-feeding, a different handler over the same interface, keeps both alive (law 4).

disintegration (Fig 6, the flagship) — playable: a scripted thermal shock collapses viability, halts viability-gated metabolism, and turns biomass into molecular debris, watchable step by step. Structural: the same metabolic-exchange interface is realized at three grains (coarse lumped yield, saturating kinetic, real COBRApy flux-balance over e_coli_core) behind ports that never move — the cell-to-molecular-network grain-swap (law 4).

molecular-interfaces (Fig 7) — an F1Fo ATP-synthase mechanism drives all four physical channels (chemical, electrical, mechanical, thermal) from one coupled proton flux, honoring the interface at a molecular grain of the kind disintegration drops into.

biomolecular-complementarity (Fig 8) — a six-level nested place graph (membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, chromosome, chromatin, nucleosome) with a coupled gene-expression cascade wired to the deepest leaf; the interface is preserved through the deepest nesting in this codebase (law 2). Complementarity/selectivity is narrated, not built — hierarchical assembly is demonstrated, binding selectivity is not.

autopoiesis (Fig 9) — metabolism, containment, and replication compile into mutual closure toward a minimal cell, a second worked example of law 4''s grain-swap; demonstrates the closure pattern qualitatively, not a validated autopoietic system.

growth-and-division (Fig 10a,b) — growth (an autocatalytic, energy-coupled process) drives the cell's own DNA past a threshold; crossing it fires a genuine place-graph rewrite, one cell node becoming two, mass conserved (the parent is halved, not duplicated) — law 2' (rewrite conformance) alongside law 2 (interface preserved across the rewrite).

development-and-evolution (Fig 10c-f) — biofilm nesting and port-addition/selection compile and run as event-driven rewrites, including a genuine node-inserting "Live Topology" pair for each; explicitly caveated (gate: needs_calibration) — selection is a single fixed-constant ODE and the new port a scripted ramp, per the paper's own "open and substantial challenge."
evidence_against: The handlers are toy-real, not calibrated — plausible constants, not fitted ones — so the dynamics demonstrate the *pattern* (niche construction, viability collapse, closure, genuine rewrite) rather than a quantitatively validated cell.

Conformance is structural only (port names, types, wiring) — the compiler does not check units, dimensions, invariants, or runtime behavior, so a handler can conform structurally while still getting the biology wrong.
The capstone whole cell is assembled by hand in the figures' style (wholecell.py), not emitted by the compiler from the studies' own drafts.
development-and-evolution's own gate is needs_calibration: its selection and port-addition dynamics are honestly labeled scripted stand-ins, not emergent population or fitness mechanisms.
caveats: Two layers, read deliberately: the draft composites are inert (ports + contract, no dynamics) and are rendered in loom; the executable composites run and are shown as dynamics figures. A study's draft render and its executable dynamics are the same interface at two stages, not two different models.

The compiler is the binding stage only — it installs a conforming mechanism per draft; it does not fit parameters or invent mechanisms. Conformance is structural (port names, types, wiring), not behavioral — it does not check units, dimensions, invariants, or runtime behavior.

The capstone whole cell (see below) is assembled by hand in the figures' style, not emitted by the compiler from any study's drafts. Its division conserves mass (the mother is halved, not doubled) and its death is a scripted thermal shock, not an emergent failure.

development-and-evolution is deliberately the most caveated study in the investigation (gate: needs_calibration) — read its own study.yaml before citing its results as more than a pattern demonstration.

studies.name: cellular-interface
studies.title: The Cellular Interface
studies.question: Can the cellular boundary be specified as nothing but typed, unit-bearing exchange ports (chemical mol·s⁻¹, mechanical N, electrical C·s⁻¹, thermal J·s⁻¹) plus higher-level variables (growth, shape, objective, viability) — with no committed mechanism — and compiled, by installing one conforming handler, into a bounded, goal-directed cell whose interface is exactly the one declared?

findings.statement: Installing one conforming handler grows the cell through its interface. Confirmed: shape 1.0 → 4.2.
The cell takes up chemical across its interface (net negative flux). Confirmed: chemical flux 0.0 → -0.8.
The cell makes progress toward its declared objective as growth proceeds. Confirmed: objective 0.0 → 1.6.

Law 1 (conformance) is machine-checked at compile time: a handler whose declared ports do not match the draft signature is rejected with a CompileError naming the missing ports. The one concrete impostor in the codebase, `NonConformingMetabolism`, breaks the metabolism interface used by the disintegration/Fig 6 study (not a cellular-interface-specific contract), but it is the mechanical proof that the compiler enforces the same Law-1 structural check for any declared interface, including this one — no cellular-interface-specific impostor exists, and none is claimed here.

evidence.observed: compile_composite raises CompileError; the message names the missing "biomass" and "secretions" ports
evidence.discovered_during: authoring this study — cross-referenced from the disintegration/Fig 6 codebase, not run as part of this study's own baselines

expected.summary: Law 1 conformance predicts any handler whose ports diverge from the declared signature is refused at compile time.

studies.claim: The cell's interface is authored as an inert typed contract and compiled to a running bounded cell; a non-conforming handler that breaks the port contract is rejected at compile time with a CompileError naming the missing ports (Law 1 conformance).

biological_validation.basis: The interface tests (shape, chemical, objective) all pass on measured readouts; the inert-draft sanity check stays at its 1.0 shape seed, isolating the installed handler as the cause. Law 1 conformance is confirmed mechanically by an existing test in the metabolism-interface codebase (cross-referenced honestly, not claimed as cellular-interface-specific).

regression_compatibility.basis: The Fig 4a and Fig 4b composites build and fig04b-executable runs to completion (scripts/build_executables.py + scripts/measure_all.py, 2026-08-16).

explanatory_gain.basis: Compiling the inert Fig 4 interface into a running, bounded, goal-directed cell makes structural conformance (Law 1) and interface preservation directly observable, and separates the interface-specification claim from the mechanism-independence claim now homed in disintegration/Fig 6.

derived.insight: Installing one conforming handler grows the cell through its interface. Confirmed: shape 1.0 → 4.2.

studies.name: cell-environment-coupling
studies.title: Cell–Environment Coupling
studies.question: Does the cellular interface become a genuine sense/act loop when the environment is a real diffusing spatial field the cell reads and acts back on?

findings.statement: The Fig 4 interface closes into a genuine coupling: the cell senses the field at its location and draws it down by taking up matter. Confirmed: uptake flux 0.0 → 0.34, bolus cell 1.0 → 0.2 — the cell measurably reshapes the gradient it depends on (niche construction).
The cell acts back mechanically on its environment — sensing and acting are one coupling over the shared field store, not two subsystems. Confirmed: traction 0.0 → 0.41.
The cell drives a mechanical field in the shared environment store. Confirmed: mechanical field 0.0 → 0.94.

studies.claim: Compiling the Fig 5 draft installs a real Laplacian-diffusion field and single-cell uptake; the cell depletes nutrient locally, diffusion refills it, and the cell reshapes the very gradient it depends on (niche construction) — interface preserved (Law 2).

biological_validation.basis: The coupling tests (uptake, traction, mechanical field) all pass on measured readouts against a real diffusing 9-cell lattice.

regression_compatibility.basis: The Fig 5 composite builds and fig05-executable runs to completion (scripts/build_executables.py + scripts/measure_all.py, 2026-08-16).

explanatory_gain.basis: Closing the Fig 4 interface into a Fig 5 sense/act loop over a real diffusing field makes "sensing and acting are one coupling, not two" and niche construction directly observable, behind an interface preserved unchanged (Law 2).

derived.insight: The Fig 4 interface closes into a genuine coupling: the cell senses the field at its location and draws it down by taking up matter. Confirmed: uptake flux 0.0 → 0.34, bolus cell 1.0 → 0.2 — the cell measurably reshapes the gradient it depends on (niche construction).

studies.name: cell-cell-coupling
studies.title: Cell–Cell Coupling
studies.question: When two cell interfaces are coupled through one shared environmental nutrient store, what is coupled is not only state but constraint — does one cell's uptake push the other outside its viable bounds (competition), and can a different handler over the same coupling interface stabilize both (cross-feeding)?

findings.statement: Coupling two cells through one shared nutrient store couples constraint, not just state: under competition, the cell with lower uptake capacity (cell_b, vmax 0.2) is driven out of its viable band while the stronger cell (cell_a, vmax 0.8) persists. Confirmed: cell_a viability 1.0 → 1.0, cell_b viability 1.0 → 0.0001.

evidence.observed: cell_a viability stays 1.0; cell_b viability collapses to 0.0001; env.nutrient depleted 1.0 → 0.1999

findings.statement: A different handler over the same coupling interface (cross-feeding: symmetric vmax, partial byproduct return to the shared pool) sustains both cells — the constraint negotiated over one shared store is not fixed by the interface, it is set by which handler occupies it. Confirmed: both cell_a and cell_b viability 1.0 → 1.0 under cross-feeding.

evidence.observed: cell_a and cell_b viability both 1.0; env.nutrient settles at 0.538 (vs 0.1999 under competition)

findings.statement: The competitive asymmetry and the cross-feeding symmetry live entirely in the handler env layer, never in the draft or the interface — confirming law 4 (handler independence over one coupling interface) and law 2 (interface preserved) simultaneously. Confirmed structurally: interface_of(compete) == interface_of(crossfeed) == interface_of(draft).

evidence.observed: identical compiled interface across both handler envs and the inert draft (tests/test_cellcell.py::test_handler_independence_same_interface)

studies.claim: Two cells over one shared-nutrient interface negotiate viability, not just state: under competition the weaker cell (lower uptake capacity) is driven below its viable band while the stronger persists (cell_a viability → 1.0, cell_b → ~0.0001); under cross-feeding, the same coupling interface with a different handler keeps both cells viable (cell_a and cell_b → 1.0) — two handler environments over one interface (Law 4), the draft itself unchanged (Law 2).

biological_validation.basis: Competition drives the weaker cell (lower uptake capacity) below its viable band while the stronger persists, and the shared pool is measurably depleted (coupling is real); cross-feeding over the same interface keeps both cells viable. All three tests plus the interface-preservation control pass.

regression_compatibility.basis: All three cellcell composites build and both executables run to completion (scripts/build_executables.py entries cellcell-compete / cellcell-crossfeed; tests/test_cellcell.py, 3 passed).

explanatory_gain.basis: Making the same two-draft-role composite negotiate two different viability outcomes purely by swapping the handler env (competition vs cross-feeding) makes "coupling through a shared store couples constraint, not just state" concrete, and demonstrates law 4 (handler independence) directly.

derived.insight: Coupling two cells through one shared nutrient store couples constraint, not just state: under competition, the cell with lower uptake capacity (cell_b, vmax 0.2) is driven out of its viable band while the stronger cell (cell_a, vmax 0.8) persists. Confirmed: cell_a viability 1.0 → 1.0, cell_b viability 1.0 → 0.0001.

studies.name: disintegration
studies.title: Disintegration
studies.question: Fig 6 is disintegration — the change in level of description that fires when a cell crosses its viability bound. Two faces: (a) played through, does the disintegration composite actually show that shift — a thermal shock pushing viability past its bound, viability collapsing, viability-gated metabolism halting, and biomass turning into molecular debris? (b) Is the metabolic-exchange interface at the heart of that same shift realizable at a coarse cell-level grain, an intermediate kinetic grain, and a resolved molecular-network grain (real COBRApy flux-balance optimization) — three grains behind ports that never move?

findings.statement: Played through, `fig06-disintegration-dynamics` shows the cell→molecular level shift: a scripted thermal shock pushes the cell past its viability bound and viability collapses. Confirmed: viability 1.0 → ~0 over 20 steps.

evidence.observed: viability starts >0.9, collapses to ~0 by step 20 after the t≈8 thermal shock

findings.statement: Once viability collapses, viability-gated metabolism halts and biomass converts into molecular debris — the level shift is not just a number crossing a threshold, it is mass moving from the cell-level state (biomass) to the molecular-level state (debris). Confirmed: debris 0 → ~4.6.
The linear coarse-grain handler drives the shared metabolic-exchange interface to biomass 4.0. Confirmed: coarse → biomass 4.0 (energy 2.4, entropy 0.8, secretions 1.6).

The Michaelis–Menten handler reaches a distinct endpoint on the identical interface — same ports, different mechanism, different trajectory (law 4), directly asserted by test_fig6_handler_independence. Confirmed: kinetic → biomass 2.667.

studies.name: biomolecular-complementarity
studies.title: Biomolecular Complementarity
studies.question: Do molecular mechanisms compose into nested hierarchical composites (proteins -> complexes -> organelles -> ECM) whose interfaces survive deep nesting, and does a gene-expression cascade wired to the deepest leaves preserve every interface across six levels (Law 2 at the deepest nesting)?

findings.statement: Metabolism feeds the cascade from the membrane inward, each observable rising from zero. Confirmed: nutrients 0 -> 2.4, metabolites 0 -> 1.5, energy 0 -> 0.84.
DNA nested five levels down the place graph is transcribed into a small mRNA pool, and translated into a small protein pool. Confirmed: mRNA 0 -> 0.178, protein 0 -> 0.008.

The interface is preserved and actively driven all the way to the deepest leaf: the ribosome pool, nested six levels down in a parallel organelles branch (cytoplasm.organelles.ribosomal_complex.ribosome), is maintained against dilution by the subunit-assembly loop rather than merely sitting untouched at its seed. Confirmed: ribosome ~0.5 -> ~0.501, structurally wired and dynamically maintained.

Honesty point: complementarity/selectivity — which molecular partners bind, and why not others — is the paper's organizing principle for why this hierarchy assembles, but it is not a mechanism this executable implements or tests. Every handler reads and writes a fixed, pre-declared store path; there is no binding-affinity calculation, no competing partner, and no non-cognate binder that gets rejected. What is demonstrated is hierarchical assembly (a six-level nested place graph that compiles, resolves every leaf, and carries coupled dynamics from its deepest node outward), not fitted binding selectivity. This study does not claim a selectivity mechanism that was not built.

evidence.observed: no handler in handlers_fig08.py computes a binding affinity, evaluates competing partners, or rejects a non-cognate binder; every input/output is a fixed store path
evidence.discovered_during: authoring this study — verified directly against handlers_fig08.py, not asserted from the paper''s narrative alone

Complementarity/selectivity is the paper''s organizing principle for why molecules assemble into this hierarchy, but the executable demonstrates hierarchical assembly, not fitted binding selectivity — no partner-choice or binding-affinity mechanism is built or claimed.

studies.name: autopoiesis
studies.title: Autopoiesis — Composition of the Cellular Interface
studies.question: How does a maintained cellular interface arise from molecular processes? Do metabolism, containment, and replication, mutually wired so each maintains the others, compile into a self-sustaining minimal cell — and does each self-organized function run at coarse, self-organized, and molecular grains behind one interface (Law 4, its second home)?

findings.statement: Containment is realized by three distinct conforming handlers at three grains (coarse closure, self-organized process, molecular mechanism) behind one compiled Fig 9a interface — Law 4's second worked example after Fig 6. Confirmed: all three grains produce non-identical numeric dynamics from the shared lipid driver (boundary 0→1.5, membrane 0→2.0, aggregate 0→1.0).

The minimal cell's enzyme pool exists only because gene expression made it — metabolism cannot flux from a seeded enzyme pool, only from a produced one. Confirmed: enzymes.concentration climbs 0 → 0.95, the qualitative signature of the closure pattern (not a validated autopoietic criterion).

Metabolism's energy output is spent by replication to grow the gene pool — the two functions are coupled through a produced quantity (energy), not independent drivers. Confirmed: genes.concentration climbs 1.0 → 1.69 as energy.energy climbs 1.0 → 1.31.

Sanity check on the framework's definition: the inert fig09b-minimal-cell draft, with no mechanism, has an empty update and stays at seed. Confirmed: inert-draft enzymes.concentration stays 0.0 (fails the closure threshold by design — the definition of a draft, not a scientific control).

evidence.observed: inert draft enzymes.concentration stays 0.0 (empty update by construction)

studies.claim: The three closure processes (metabolism, containment, replication) compile into a minimal cell whose interface is produced by the coupling itself — enzymes and energy exist only because a coupled process made them, not because they were seeded — and each function is realized by conforming handlers at multiple grains (containment and replication at three, metabolism at two) behind one fixed interface, Law 4''s second worked example. This is the closure pattern demonstrated qualitatively, not a validated autopoietic system.

biological_validation.basis: PASS at the toy-real, qualitative level only: the Maturana-Varela closure pattern is demonstrated (enzymes and energy exist only because a coupled process made them; a coupled function cannot flux from a seeded pool), and containment/replication genuinely instantiate multiple conforming grains behind one interface. This is not a validated autopoietic system — no boundary-maintenance, steady-state, or perturbation-recovery criterion from the literature is applied.

regression_compatibility.basis: All four fig09a/fig09b composites build (tests/test_composites_build.py::test_composite_builds, parametrized over every *.composite.json stem) and both fig09a-executable and fig09b-executable run to completion with interface preservation confirmed (tests/test_compilation.py::test_env_conforms_compiles_and_runs).

explanatory_gain.basis: Watching enzymes and energy climb from zero — produced by one process before another can use them — makes the closure idea concrete rather than asserted, and containment's three genuinely-distinct grains behind one interface gives Law 4 a second worked example beyond Fig 6.

Confirmed: all three grains produce non-identical numeric dynamics from the shared lipid driver (boundary 0→1.5, membrane 0→2.0, aggregate 0→1.0).

studies.name: development-and-evolution
studies.title: Development and Evolution
studies.question: Fig 10c–f asks whether two of biology's hardest structural transitions — development (individual cells nesting into a collective composite, a biofilm, with its own shared interface) and evolution (a new interface port switching on, selected by viability) — can be represented as event-driven, compositional rewrites (Law 2′) that preserve the interface underneath them (Law 2). Two composites answer the first half of that (do the drafts compile to executables that run, behind an unchanged interface?) faithfully. This study asks the harder, second half explicitly: how much of what runs is a genuine developmental/evolutionary mechanism, versus a scripted stand-in — and is honest that the paper itself calls this transition "an open and substantial challenge" (line 580).

findings.statement: Development's continuous path compiles to an executable that grows a shared, collective biofilm interface (biofilm_mass 0 → 3.09) behind an interface preserved exactly across compilation. Partial: this demonstrates the compositional pattern of individual cells folding into a collective interface, but the growth is a continuous scalar (ODE-updated population/mass), not discrete cell-node insertion, and no biological calibration is claimed.

evidence.observed: biofilm_mass 0 → 3.09; ecm 0 → 2.47; attached 0 → 1.85; adhesion 0 → 0.93; cells 1.00 → 2.09 (10 steps)

findings.statement: Evolution's continuous path switches on a previously-silent chemical exchange port (new_port 0 → 0.65) that the ancestral cell lacks. Partial: the mechanics of "a new interface capability arises" are represented, but the switch-on is an unconditional, config-driven first-order ramp — not an emergent consequence of variation or selection acting on a population.

Evolution's continuous path grows the ancestral population (cell_ecoli.cell_count 1 → 4) under a viability-weighted selection term. Partial: this is a single ODE with viability and fitness held at fixed constants — not real fitness-based population dynamics, competition between variants, or drift.

Two distinct idioms answer "can development/evolution be a compositional rewrite?" differently, and they should not be conflated. The compiled/executable path (fig10-2-executable, fig10-3-executable) uses ordinary Process handlers behind a preserved interface — no place-graph rewrite occurs there. A separate Live-Topology pair (fig10-2-rewrite, fig10-3-rewrite) genuinely inserts and removes place-graph nodes at runtime via an `overwrite[tree[node]]` output (biofilm colonization to capacity 5 then ECM secretion per cell; a mutant lineage sweep that prunes the wildtype to zero) — closer in spirit to Fig 10-1's division rewrite, but driven by a fixed wall-clock schedule and a hardcoded mutant fitness advantage (1.6), not by the community's own state.

evidence.smoking_gun: meta_modelers_guide/fig10_topology.py (BiofilmDevelopment, LineageEvolution) vs meta_modelers_guide/handlers_fig10.py (SurfaceAttachmentProc et al., ordinary Process subclasses, no RewriteHandler)
evidence.observed: fig10-2-rewrite: cell count climbs monotonically 1 → 5, then ECM nodes appear only once the community is full; fig10-3-rewrite: mutant count ≥ 2 and organism count = 0 by the final frame, total population bounded ≤ 6

findings.statement: Even the genuinely node-inserting Live-Topology composites are scripted, not emergent: the biofilm colonizes on a fixed timer (grow_every=2.0) up to a fixed capacity (5), and the evolution mutant appears at a hardcoded time (mutate_at=4.0) with a hardcoded fitness advantage (1.6) rather than one derived from a fitness landscape. Neither trigger is gated by the composite's own internal state, unlike Fig 10-1's division (gated by DNA crossing a threshold).

evidence.discovered_during: reading meta_modelers_guide/fig10_topology.py::BiofilmDevelopment.update / LineageEvolution.update against DivisionRewrite in handlers_fig10.py

studies.claim: Development nests individual cells into a biofilm collective behind a preserved, shared extracellular-matrix interface (Law 2), and evolution switches on a new chemical port under a viability-weighted growth term — both compile and run, and a separate "Live Topology" pair for each even performs genuine runtime place-graph node insertion/removal (in the spirit of Law 2′). But — the defining point of this study — none of this is a validated biological result: selection is a single ODE with fixed viability/fitness constants (not real fitness-based population dynamics), the "new port" is a first-order config-driven ramp (not an emergent evolutionary innovation), the continuous-path biofilm state is a pre-declared, non-inserted scalar store, and even the genuine node-inserting Live-Topology composites run on a fixed wall-clock schedule with a hardcoded mutant fitness advantage rather than an emergent, state-driven trigger. The paper itself calls development and evolution "an open and substantial challenge" (line 580); this study demonstrates the pattern, not the phenomenon.

biological_validation.basis: The paper itself calls development and evolution "an open and substantial challenge" (line 580); this study does not attempt to close that gap. Selection is a single ODE with fixed viability/fitness constants, the new port is a config-driven ramp, the continuous biofilm state is a pre-declared scalar store, and even the genuinely node-inserting Live-Topology composites run on a hardcoded schedule with a hardcoded mutant fitness advantage. Every primary behavior_test passes as a pattern demonstration; none is a validated biological result.

regression_compatibility.basis: All 6 baseline composites build (tests/test_composites_build.py::test_composite_builds) and fig10-2-executable / fig10-3-executable run to completion with the interface preserved exactly against their drafts (tests/test_compilation.py::test_env_conforms_compiles_and_runs).

explanatory_gain.basis: Separating the "compiles and runs behind a preserved interface" claim from the "genuinely rewrites the place graph" claim — and showing that Fig 10c–f actually contains both idioms, neither one biologically calibrated — is itself the useful result: it locates exactly where this framework's toy stand-ins for development and evolution sit, and what would need to change (state-gated triggers, a real fitness landscape, heritable variation) to make them more than a pattern demonstration.

derived.insight: Development's continuous path compiles to an executable that grows a shared, collective biofilm interface (biofilm_mass 0 → 3.09) behind an interface preserved exactly across compilation. Partial: this demonstrates the compositional pattern of individual cells folding into a collective interface, but the growth is a continuous scalar (ODE-updated population/mass), not discrete cell-node insertion, and no biological calibration is claimed.
